title: PRODUCT_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md still self-declares RATIFIED while half of it is retired -- and six shipped source files cite it as the design authority
repro: design -- read docs/redesign/PRODUCT_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:3-4 ('RATIFIED ... the single document every teammate obeys'), then implement its sec1-sec2 palette: you ship amber #d89a4e on a warm #1a1814 ramp. The live system is pure-neutral #161616 + peach #fab283 (styles/tokens.css:35,54).
evidence: docs/redesign/PRODUCT_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:3-4,13-21,48-64,75-81,117-124,133-147,312-314; superseded by styles/tokens.css:1-26, docs/redesign/R9_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:79 ('The R6 Pure Black doctrine stands'), docs/redesign/VYSTED_DESIGN.md:17-20, DECISIONS.md:43-45 (D26/D27/D28). Live code citing the doc as authority: styles/tokens.css:21, src/app/globals.css:39,199,231, src/components/DataTable.tsx, src/modules/chat/SuggestionChips.tsx, src/modules/notes/NotesToolbar.tsx, src/store/workspace.ts.
notes: Mechanism: the doc is HALF alive -- sec1-sec7 (color ramp, accent hex, control scale sm32/md40/lg48, weights 510/590, radius-panel 6px, type scale 11/12/13/15/18/22) were reversed by R6+R9, while sec8 and sec11-sec16 (EmptyState, DataTable, Tiptap toolbar, composer, palette, the off-scale audit) are STILL the live authority and are the reason shipped files link to it. Nothing marks the boundary, and DECISIONS.md/CHANGELOG.md contain NO entry for the Warm-Graphite -> Pure-Black reversal at all (DECISIONS.md jumps R8:5 -> R9:39; grep of CHANGELOG.md for 'Warm Graphite|Pure Black|OpenCode|#fab283' = 0 hits). Consequence for a public 0.9.0: the first outside contributor who follows the repo's own cited taste authority ships the retired palette, and no one can answer 'why peach and not amber' from the record. Smallest fix: a 4-line SUPERSEDED banner at PRODUCT_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:1 naming which sections are dead (sec0-sec7) and which still bind (sec8, sec11-sec16) + pointers to VYSTED_DESIGN.md and R9_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md, plus one DECISIONS.md row recording the reversal.

title: 44 CSS var() fallbacks in globals.css are frozen at retired R4 values, contradicting the file's own stated invariant (FR-030 'every fallback hex')
repro: design -- grep 'var(--color-' src/app/globals.css and diff each fallback against styles/tokens.css: 27 color fallbacks and 17 non-color fallbacks disagree with the token they back. e.g. src/app/globals.css:201 'box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-amber-400, #d89a4e)' backs a token whose value is #fab283.
evidence: src/app/globals.css:18-20 (the claimed invariant: 'Fallbacks use NEUTRAL values so a missing token degrades to the same neutral gray -- never warm, never blue'); violating lines: :76,:189,:201,:202,:208,:209,:222,:237,:287,:289,:295,:302,:303,:320,:346,:347,:348,:349,:350,:351,:352,:353,:354,:355,:444,:502,:511 (color) and :73,:242,:244,:249,:251,:255,:257,:301,:304,:383,:421,:519 (non-color: --font-weight-heading 590 vs token 700 at styles/tokens.css:124; --radius-panel 0.375rem vs token 0 at styles/tokens.css:145; --text-panel-title 0.9375rem vs token 0.8125rem at styles/tokens.css:117). Authority for the rule: docs/redesign/PRODUCT_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:83-89 (FR-030 lockstep, 'and every fallback hex') and CLAUDE.md's chart-theme lockstep gotcha.
notes: Verified NOT a rendering bug today: compiled src/app/globals.css through @tailwindcss/postcss 4.3.0 and every referenced theme var is emitted on :root (--color-amber-400, --color-charcoal-900, --radius-panel, --font-weight-heading, --text-panel-title, --color-lume all EMITTED), so no fallback currently fires. The defect is that the file's load-bearing comment is false and the fallbacks are a palette LIE at exactly the surface the project's own lockstep rule names: a maintainer grepping globals.css for the accent finds the retired amber #d89a4e three times (:201,:208,:222) and the retired warm panel #1a1814 (:346,:444). Same freeze produced src/app/globals.css:231, which still calls the live type scale 'the Warm Graphite type scale' -- a name PRODUCT_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:19-21 retired. Smallest fix: one sweep re-valuing all 44 fallbacks from styles/tokens.css (or deleting the fallbacks, since the tokens are proven always-emitted), plus a 20-line check in scripts/audit-design-tokens.mjs that fails when a var() fallback disagrees with its token -- otherwise the next reskin refreezes them.

title: --color-warning is documented as 'stale data' but carries at least seven unrelated meanings, several with no label
repro: design -- the same yellow #e0a13a means 'this price is stale/synthetic' (src/components/DataBadges.tsx:57), 'Docker not found' (src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:744), 'your keybinding conflicts' (:1482), 'plugin is initializing' (src/components/PluginManagerPanel.tsx:136), 'agent run paused' (src/modules/chat/AgentsRail.tsx:96), 'budget exhausted' (:134) and 'no chart data' (src/modules/chart/ChartPanel.tsx:1385).
evidence: styles/tokens.css:83 ('stale / paper / caution badge'); src/components/DataBadges.tsx:17 ('--color-warning is documented as "stale data"'); unlabelled uses: src/components/StatusChrome.tsx:208 ('bg-warning animate-pulse' -- a bare dot), src/modules/chat/AgentsRail.tsx:134 ('bg-warning' -- a bare bar), src/modules/chart/ChartPanel.tsx:1385 (glyph, title-attribute only); promise text at docs/redesign/PRODUCT_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:92-93 ('only ever appears as a labelled badge ("STALE"/"PAPER")').
notes: Mechanism: one semantic token absorbed every caution meaning in the app, so the strongest data-honesty signal the product has (FR-041 synthetic/stale provenance) is rendered in the same yellow as an infrastructure nag. Two of the uses are colour-only with no adjacent text, which also fails the colour-is-not-the-only-channel rule. Concrete consequence for a finance terminal: a user who learns 'yellow = my number may be wrong' then sees yellow on a plugin row and learns to discount it. Smallest fix: keep --color-warning for data provenance only and add one --color-caution (or reuse charcoal-400 + an icon) for infrastructure/lifecycle states; give the three unlabelled uses a text or aria label.
